find.note: Call with Northwind Freight, 12 March. Attendees: Head of IR, Head of Sustainability; two analysts on our side. We opened on the fleet transition. The company converted 140 urban delivery vans to electric last year and is pleased with their uptime. On targets, the Head of Sustainability confirmed that Northwind will submit its near-term emissions targets to the SBTi for validation before the end of this year. We asked whether they would also commit to a 2040 net zero date; they said the board is looking at it but would not give a timeline. On disclosure, IR said the company will publish its first standalone TCFD report alongside the 2025 annual report. We raised driver safety and subcontractor working hours; management described its current audit programme and did not propose any change. Follow-up: check the SBTi submission in Q4.
key_phrases: submit its near-term emissions targets to the SBTi
publish its first standalone TCFD report

find.note: Meeting with Halden Mining chair and company secretary, London, 3 April. Topic: tailings and community relations at the Copper Ridge site. The chair noted that the main dam was reclassified after the 2023 independent review and that there were no incidents last year. We pressed for an independent human rights impact assessment at Copper Ridge, given the complaints from the downstream villages. The chair agreed that the company will commission an independent human rights impact assessment of Copper Ridge and publish a summary by mid-2026. We also asked for conformance reports against the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management for every site; the company secretary said they hope to get there eventually. On board composition, the chair mentioned that two directors with mine safety experience joined in 2024. Constructive overall; we will track the assessment.
key_phrases: will commission an independent human rights impact assessment

find.note: Call with Brightwater Utilities IR, 20 May. We asked about the coal phase-out date for the Elm Point plant. IR said the company remains committed to a responsible transition and that the timing depends on the next regulatory rate case, which they expect to file at some point next year. We asked whether they would set a methane intensity target for the gas distribution business; IR said they would pass the request on to management. They highlighted that renewables reached 31% of generation in 2024, up from 24%, and that two coal units have been retired since 2020. We asked for a review of whether their trade association lobbying matches their climate position; no view was given. Next step: request a meeting with the chair before the AGM.

Meeting with Corvane Pharma compensation committee chair and General Counsel, 9 January. Follow-up to our vote against last year's say-on-pay resolution, which received 61% support. The committee chair walked through the changes. First, the company will add a relative TSR modifier to the 2026 performance share awards. Second, the one-off retention grant made to the CEO in 2024 will not be repeated, and the committee will not make further one-off awards to the CEO before 2028. Third, the General Counsel said Corvane will disclose the bonus scorecard targets and outcomes in this year's remuneration report. We asked them to raise the CEO shareholding requirement from 300% to 500% of salary; the chair said the committee would reflect on it. They also mentioned that the board appointed a new independent director with HR experience last autumn.
key_phrases: will not make further one-off awards
disclose the bonus scorecard targets and outcomes

find.note: Call with Lumena Apparel Head of Responsible Sourcing, 14 February. Focus: wages at Tier 1 garment suppliers in Bangladesh and Cambodia. She said the company mapped all Tier 1 and 80% of Tier 2 factories last year and published the supplier list. We asked for a time-bound living wage commitment. She told us Lumena will publish a living wage gap analysis for its top 50 suppliers by the end of Q3. On a binding target, she said they aspire to close the gap over time but cannot give a date while purchasing practices are under review. We asked about the International Accord on health and safety; they renewed their signature in 2023. We flagged freedom of association concerns at one Cambodian supplier; she said she was aware of the reports.
key_phrases: publish a living wage gap analysis

find.note: Meeting with Arvent Chemicals CFO and Head of Strategy, 28 February. We discussed the credibility of the 2030 Scope 1 and 2 target (-42% versus 2021). The CFO said emissions fell 9% last year, mostly because of the closure of the Antwerp cracker. We asked how the remaining reduction will be funded. The CFO confirmed that Arvent will disclose climate-related capex as a separate line in the capital markets day materials in June. We asked for a Scope 3 target covering purchased goods; the Head of Strategy said this is under consideration given data quality. On electrification, the CFO said Arvent will sign a renewable power purchase agreement for its Rotterdam sites before year-end. We suggested linking the long-term incentive plan to the emissions target; they only noted that the board sets pay.
key_phrases: disclose climate-related capex as a separate line
sign a renewable power purchase agreement

find.note: Call with Tellus Bank sustainability lead and IR, 5 June. The bank published its first financed emissions inventory in March, covering 70% of the loan book. We asked for interim sector targets. The sustainability lead said targets for oil and gas and for power will be set and published with the half-year results in August. On the energy supply ratio, IR said the bank does not see value in the metric and will not report it. We raised the expiry of the bank's thermal coal policy at the end of this year; they said the board risk committee reviews policies regularly. IR also mentioned that the bank received an A- score from CDP last year. Next step: review the sector targets in August.
key_phrases: set and published with the half-year results

find.note: Meeting with Orrin Foods Head of Procurement, 18 September. Topic: palm oil and soy traceability ahead of the EU deforestation regulation. He said 96% of palm oil volumes are traceable to mill and that the company joined a landscape programme in Sabah in 2022. We asked for a public cut-off date for soy from the Cerrado. He said Orrin would like to align with peers but the decision sits with the group sustainability council, which next meets in November. We also asked for the grievance log to be published; he said they are open to the idea. He noted that the company already publishes its list of palm oil mills twice a year. Constructive, but nothing firm; to revisit after November.

Call with Quarry Point Software lead independent director, 11 November. We asked about board oversight of AI risk after the product incident in Q2. She said the audit committee took on AI oversight this year and has met the CTO twice. She told us the board will amend the audit committee charter to name AI risk explicitly before the next proxy statement. We asked whether the company would publish its responsible AI principles. She said yes: the company will put its responsible AI principles on the investor site within six months. We also asked for a sunset on the dual-class structure; she said the founders do not support one and the board has no plans to propose it. She added that three new directors have joined since 2022.
key_phrases: responsible AI principles on the investor site

find.note: Meeting with Valemont Hotels Chief People Officer, 2 October. Discussion of outsourced housekeeping staff at the Gulf properties. She said all labour agencies were re-audited in 2024 and that recruitment fees found at two agencies were repaid to workers. We asked Valemont to adopt the Employer Pays Principle across all regions. She confirmed that from January the company will require every labour agency contract to include the Employer Pays Principle. We asked for the audit results by country; she said that would be difficult for confidentiality reasons. She also described a wellbeing app for hotel staff launched last year. We will ask for evidence of the contract change at the next meeting.
key_phrases: every labour agency contract to include

find.note: Call with Sefton Water CEO and IR, 22 July. The CEO opened with the storm overflow figures: spills fell 18% in 2024 after the first phase of the overflow programme. We asked the board to tie executive bonuses to spill reduction; the CEO said this already happened last year, and 20% of the annual bonus is now linked to the spill metric. We asked whether the company would hold back dividends while regulatory fines are outstanding. The CEO said the board will not pay a dividend for the 2025 financial year. On leakage, IR said the company expects to keep improving but gave no target. We will check the dividend statement at the interim results.
key_phrases: will not pay a dividend for the 2025
